_comment: What the cdk8s libraries are called in Ruby.
cdk8s-plus ships one package per Kubernetes version it targets, and they
coexist: a cluster on 1.27 and one on 1.32 want different ones. Each gets
its own gem and module (CDK8sPlus27, CDK8sPlus32) so both can be installed
side by side, which is exactly how the npm packages behave.
They all depend on the same cdk8s and constructs, so publishing the set
adds eight gems and finds those two already there.
CDK8s, not Cdk8s: the name is an initialism with a digit in it, which no
casing rule is going to guess. Named explicitly so the module and every
reference to it agree.
cdk8s-plus is versioned against a Kubernetes minor (27, 28, 29 ...), and
each is a separate assembly, so each gets its own gem and module rather
than one gem that silently changes what it binds to.
